notes: Every heading and standing sentence the products use. The renderers hold only structure, so change the words here and run gwylio check. Blanks in braces, such as {count}, are filled when a product is rendered; each text may use only the blanks its schema lists (docs/schema/copy.schema.json). British English, no en or em dashes, acronyms spelled out on first use.

common.period_line: Period covered: {start} to {end}. Rendered on {generated_on} from the register as it stood that day.
common.blind_spot_rule: A blind spot is not quiet. A requirement whose evidence public sources cannot see (low or no scanability) and that has no active reports is invisible to this tool, not calm; its silence is not evidence of anything.
common.undercount: Counts of reports are not counts of impact. The register shows what surfaced publicly: at least this much, and known to undercount.

method.heading: Method note
method.runs: Scan runs started in the period: {count}. Their funnels are in the first table below.
method.no_runs: No scan run started in the period, so no candidates were collected or judged in it.
method.dispositions: Final dispositions of those runs' candidates: promoted {promoted}, rejected {rejected}, duplicate {duplicate}, reinforcement {reinforcement}, deferred {deferred}. New candidates nobody has judged yet: {undisposed}.
method.promotions: Reports created in the period: {count}, of which {non_government} ({share}) came from lanes outside government. The mainstream bias guard asks for this share: a register that skews official misses the earliest signals.
method.no_promotions: No report was created in the period, so there is no non-government share or credibility spread to report.
method.credibility: The credibility of those {count} reports, digit by digit, is in the table below. Grades inflate quietly: a consultation is a 3, however official the page.
method.instrument: Instrument version used by the period's runs: {versions}.
method.instrument_current: No run used the instrument in the period; the current instrument is version {version}.
method.blind_spots: Known blind spots, requirements this tool cannot see and holds no active report on: {codes}.
method.no_blind_spots: No requirement reads as a blind spot.
method.streetlight: The scan only finds what already talks like the requirements. Biophysical, market, technological and institutional pressures that move a requirement before any publication names it are outside its reach.

intsum.title: Operational intelligence summary (INTSUM), {period}
intsum.purpose: This monthly intelligence summary (INTSUM) records what moved in the register during the period, against the requirement set named above. It is assembled from the register and the standing copy: every sentence is a fixed form filled with counts and titles.
intsum.summary_new: New reports created in the period: {count}.
intsum.summary_state_changes: Lifecycle state changes recorded in the period: {count}.
intsum.summary_faded: Reports faded by the sweep in the period: {count}.
intsum.summary_verified: Reports verified against their source in the period: {count}.
intsum.summary_directions: Across the reports that moved, {threatens} assessments threaten a requirement, {neutral} cut both ways, {informs_baseline} inform the baseline and {supports} support.
intsum.moved_intro: Reports created or changed in the period, by well-being objective. Within each list, threats and two-way signals come first.
intsum.group_empty: Nothing moved against this objective in the period.
intsum.quiet_intro: No report on these requirements was created or changed in the period.
intsum.quiet_line: {code} {short}: {status} this period. Active reports in the register: {active}. Scanability: {scanability}.
intsum.quiet_none: Every requirement in the set saw movement in the period.
intsum.verification_intro: The date check run on {today} found {count} things to look at again. Reports affected: {reports}.
intsum.verification_none: The date check found nothing to look at again.

passed_horizon.heading: Passed event horizons
passed_horizon.meaning: The event horizon has passed and nobody has updated or verified the report since. Check what happened, then rewrite the report in dated past tense.

future_language.heading: Future-framed language
future_language.meaning: The title, summary or notes use language that rots once the date passes.

stale_verification.heading: Stale verifications
stale_verification.meaning: The report was last verified against its source too long ago.

never_verified.heading: Never verified
never_verified.meaning: The report has never been verified against its source.

strategic.title: Strategic assessment, {period}: {set_name}
purpose: This annual strategic assessment sets out the standing picture of the external signals bearing on each requirement in the set, to inform the annual prioritisation exercise.

It is assembled from the register and the standing copy: every sentence is a fixed form filled with counts and titles, and nothing in it is a recommendation. Each requirement's picture counts its active reports (emerging, tracking and reinforced); matured reports are settled context and named separately.
The questions for each well-being objective are drawn from the reports that threaten a requirement or cut both ways. They are questions about the world for the people who set priorities, not advice.
strategic.picture_intro: For each requirement: its coverage status, its active reports by direction and by state, their grading spread, its scanability in the framework's own words, and the active reports with the highest potential impact.
strategic.matured_line: Matured reports kept as settled context, not counted above: {count}.
strategic.top_intro: Highest potential impact among the active reports, threats first among equals:
strategic.questions_intro: One question for each active report that threatens a member requirement or cuts both ways, threats first.
strategic.question: What would change for {codes} if this holds: {title}?
strategic.questions_none: No active report threatens this objective or cuts both ways.
strategic.coverage_intro: The audit runs down both axes: the requirements, by the lane each report was found in, and the taxonomy, by the ecosystems, resources and hazard families the reports touch.
strategic.lane_matrix_note: Each cell counts the active reports assessed against the requirement that were found in the lane. A row's status comes from the requirement's scanability and its total, so a requirement public sources cannot see reads blind spot, never quiet.
strategic.taxonomy_note: Each node counts the active reports whose requirements expect it or whose hazards belong to it. A node no requirement expects and no report touches is a blind spot of the framework: the requirement set does not foreground it, so its silence says nothing.
